title: At 18, Blaise Pascal began building a calculator to help his father add up taxes

cover.alt: A brass box on a wooden table, with five toothed dials along the front and five small windows showing digits along the back.
cover.credit: Clermont Auvergne Métropole/Pierre Tribhou · CC BY-SA 4.0

body: In 1642 the teenage **Blaise Pascal** started work on a calculating machine to ease the work of his father, the supervisor of taxes in Rouen. On the **Pascaline**, you dial each digit with a stylus and the total appears in the windows above. Its cleverest part is the carry: when a wheel passes from 9 back to 0, a little lever called a **sautoir**, moved by gravity alone, nudges the next wheel on by one. The gears turn only one way, so the machine can only add; to subtract, the user works with nines’ complements.

slides.alt: A hand uses a thin stylus to turn the toothed dials at the front of a brass Pascaline, one after another, while the digits in the small windows along the back change.
slides.caption: A Pascaline demonstrated by the Muséum Henri-Lecoq in Clermont-Ferrand: numbers are dialled in with a stylus, and the total appears in the windows along the top.
slides.credit: Clermont Auvergne Métropole/Pierre Tribhou · CC BY-SA 4.0 · excerpt

slides.question: How many prototypes did Pascal build before he showed his machine to the public in 1645?
slides.explanation: About 50, built over three years, before he presented the device in 1645.

slides.heading: The rise and fall of the Pascaline

events.text: Pascal, aged 18, starts work on the machine
He presents it to the public
Louis XIV grants him the sole right to make calculators in France
About 20 sold; cost and complexity end production

slides.heading: Of the roughly 20 Pascalines sold, nine survive
slides.note: Two of them are in Pascal’s home town, Clermont-Ferrand

slides.question: The Pascaline’s gears turn only one way. What does that mean?
options: It can only count to nine
It has to be reset every sum
slides.explanation: With wheels that turn in one direction only, it can only add. Subtraction is done with nines’ complements, a trick that turns it into an addition.
